packs.title: Museums, Parks and Civic Places
packs.promise: Explore Providence through separate museum, landscape and civic outings.

q.s: Read one credited work through its materials and setting.
st: Choose one work in an open gallery or the museum's online collection and record its artist, date and material from the credit.
Describe one feature you can actually see, without assuming the artist's intent.
Make a short sketch or spoken comparison of that feature and the museum's interpretation.

q.s: Examine a documented house detail with its commercial history intact.
st: Choose one room, object or building detail the Rhode Island Historical Society documents.
Record the society's context for the Brown family's trade and one fact about the detail without attributing invented speech to anyone.
Write what the detail can reveal and one limit of what it can prove alone.

q.s: Read the city's topography from an open hill path.
st: Select a short open route from the city's walking map.
At a safe public viewpoint, identify one foreground landform and one distant direction, or use the city's map if visibility is poor.
Sketch the relationship between slope, path and view; do not claim a landmark you cannot identify.

packs.title: Waterplace to District Park
packs.promise: Follow downtown public spaces from Waterplace toward arts blocks and the riverfront park.

q.s: Compare a designed public basin with the waterways that enter it.
st: Choose a lawful view of the basin and note one built seating or path form.
Use the city's river project information to identify the waterway and one documented public-space purpose.
Sketch how the path frames the water, marking your observation separately from the city's plan.

q.s: Read a performance building before any show begins.
st: Identify one exterior feature that marks the building as a theater.
Read the operator's theater history and record one documented change in its use or name.
Compare the present public entrance with that historical account, keeping observation and source separate.

q.s: Compare two works while crediting their makers.
st: Choose two works in an open AS220 gallery or two currently listed works or projects on its site.
Record each artist's credit and one visible or described formal choice.
Make a side-by-side study that labels your response as interpretation, not the artist's stated intent.
